text:
Maria: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — could folks clarify the kernel roadmap decisions re: microbatching thresholds, KV eviction, and the 'drop-in ops queue' idea? Trying to scope next sprint tasks.
Ken: Good q. TL;DR: we want conservative defaults for next sprint, opt-in aggressive tuning later. @Sasha can give the kernel detail and rollout plan.
Sasha: Briefly — kernel v5 focuses on three things: prefix-aware KV cache eviction, adaptive microbatching tuned to latency SLOs, and a drop-in 'ops_queue' that buffers pre-token work to smooth high-concurrency tails. Prototype target: canary in week 4.
Priya: Nice. What will the conservative defaults actually look like? i.e., batch_size / max_wait_ms / eviction window?
Sasha: Example defaults for v5-canary:
```
# v5-canary example defaults
batching:
  microbatch_max_tokens: 2048
  microbatch_max_latency_ms: 12
  max_batch_size: 64
kv_cache:
  eviction_policy: prefix-aware
  hot_window_ms: 120000
ops_queue:
  enabled: true
  max_inflight_per_shard: 16
```
Tom: Ops_queue sounds useful, but does it add p99 latency? ops_queue could buffer work but might increase tail if misconfigured.
Ken: Short answer: small p99 delta expected for cold tails (0.5-1ms), but significant p99 improvements under bursty qps since we avoid head-of-line blocking. We'll be conservative for GA.
Maria: Rollout plan? canary -> A/B -> full? auto-fallback?
Sasha: Plan: canary on internal infra with 5% synthetic + real traffic -> validate perf/regen metrics -> expand to 25% -> staged rollout with automatic fallback on latency/regression thresholds. Fallbacks: either disable ops_queue or route customers to v4 variant.
Priya: Will there be console toggles / per-customer overrides? ops teams will want quick switches.
Sasha: Yes — console feature flag + per-customer override. Also `redwoodctl` toggle: `redwoodctl runtime set-feature ops_queue=off --customer=<id>`.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled for 2026-05-12T02:30Z (job #3245).
Tom: Please surface these metrics in dashboards: microbatch latency (p50/p95/p99), kv_evictions/sec, ops_queue_queue_depth, and failed_fallbacks.
Ken: Agreed. Action: add dashboards and alerts. @Sasha to draft the alert thresholds, @Maria to coordinate customer-facing comms.
Sasha: I'll open a short RFC with the canary config + perf expectations and a PR with the config snippet above. Assigning the RFC to myself and reviewers: Ken, Priya.
Maria: I'll own the communication plan and post a short note in #product-announce when canary starts. Also will prepare an FAQ for customers about per-customer overrides.
Priya: Can you include a short example of how customers can opt out? e.g., `X-Feature-Ops-Queue: off` header or console toggle screenshot.
Sasha: Yep — will add both examples to the RFC.
Tom: One ops ask: add a readout for current eviction pressure per-shard so SRE can preemptively tune hot_window_ms.
Sasha: Good call — will add `eviction_pressure` metric and a dashboard tile.
Ken: Thanks all. Quick next steps summary: Sasha opens RFC + PR (end of week), SRE/observability team adds dashboards/alerts (Tom + ops), Maria crafts comms, Priya reviews defaults. We'll reconvene in the runtime weekly and set the canary date officially after dashboards are ready.
Maria: Great — thanks. I'll ping when comms draft is ready. :thumbsup:
Sasha: Thanks — RFC coming shortly :memo:
Tom: Adding the dashboard tickets now.
Maria: End of thread.
